data.title: Healthcare Triangle Faces Nasdaq Delisting After Bid-Price Breach
data.description:
Healthcare Triangle ( (HCTI) ) just unveiled an update.

On October 1, 2026, Healthcare Triangle, Inc. received a notice from Nasdaq’s Listing Qualifications Department stating that the company is not in compliance with the minimum $1.00 bid price requirement for continued listing on the Nasdaq Capital Market. Because Healthcare Triangle executed a 1-for-249 reverse split in August 2025 and a 1-for-60 reverse split in February 2026, it crossed Nasdaq’s cumulative reverse split threshold and is ineligible for the usual 180-day grace period.

As a result, Nasdaq issued a Staff Delisting Determination, and Healthcare Triangle’s securities are subject to delisting unless it appeals by October 8, 2026. If no appeal is made, trading would be suspended on October 12, 2026 and the shares removed from Nasdaq registration, though the company plans to request a hearing to present a compliance plan that may include another reverse stock split.

data.description:
Gold.com ( (GOLD) ) has provided an announcement.

On September 29, 2026, Gold.com, Inc. executed a Second Amended and Restated Uncommitted Credit Facility Agreement with CIBC Bank USA and other lenders, replacing its prior credit arrangements from August 21, 2025 and February 13, 2026. The new facility converts the existing agreement into an uncommitted revolving line of credit payable on demand, reduces the maximum borrowing capacity from $427.5 million to $250 million, and modifies key terms that govern the company’s funding flexibility.

The revised agreement removes several restrictions, caps, and covenants on dividends, share repurchases, acquisitions, investments, precious metal repurchase arrangements, and secured metals leases, subject to specified conditions. It also raises limits on inventory locations, inventory in transit, and major counterparty exposures, signaling a shift toward greater operational and capital allocation flexibility for Gold.com while operating with a smaller overall credit facility.
